headline: Rate base growth lifts EPS; guidance reaffirmed
summary_short: Con Edison's Q2 2026 GAAP and adjusted EPS both rose to $0.83, up 22.1% y/y, on higher CECONY electric and gas rate base; revenue was $4,069M (+13.2% y/y). Management reaffirmed full-year adjusted EPS guidance of $6.00-$6.20 and declared its 52nd consecutive annual dividend increase.
summary_long: CECONY's higher electric and gas rate base, favorable rate-increase billing timing, lower O&M expense, lower other interest expense and higher AFUDC income added $0.18 to EPS y/y, partly offset by dilution from new share issuance; O&R and Con Edison Transmission were roughly flat. Q/q comparisons look sharply negative only because Q1 2026 included a non-recurring $0.37/share gain on the sale of Con Edison's MVP equity interest, which does not recur in Q2. The company reaffirmed 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $6.00-$6.20 and declared an 88.75-cent quarterly dividend, its 52nd consecutive annual increase. At June 30, 2026, total assets were $76,459M, long-term debt $26,843M and equity $25,719M; CECONY issued $1,300M of long-term debt in the quarter.

drivers.explanation: CECONY's EPS rose $0.18 y/y on higher electric and gas rate base and rate-increase billing timing, lower O&M expense, lower other interest expense and higher AFUDC income, partly offset by dilution from new share issuance.
Same CECONY rate base growth, lower O&M and lower interest expense that lifted EPS also drove net income higher, per the company's per-subsidiary EPS variance walk.

Company reaffirmed FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $6.00-$6.20, citing continued regulated rate base growth (8.8% five-year CAGR) under constructive New York and New Jersey rate plans, and declared its 52nd consecutive annual dividend increase.
